editorial:
Imagine being so in love that you would pay a fortune to cheat death. That is exactly what happens here. You follow an older couple, Hermann and Anna, who are terrified of losing each other to old age and sickness. They find a company called Menzana that can put their minds into younger, healthy bodies. It sounds like a dream come true, but there is a huge catch. They only get to be in control for 20 hours a day. For the other four hours, the original owners of the bodies wake up and take over. It creates this weird, tense vibe where you are always wondering what the host bodies are doing while the main couple is asleep.

The acting is solid and really makes you feel the desperation of the couple. The slow build-up of tension is great, though the pace might feel a bit slow for some people. You will love how the movie asks if eternal life is actually worth the cost. If you want to see it, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a quiet night in when you want something that makes you think.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with a dark twist about the cost of this technology. You find out that the balance of power shifts as the hosts start fighting back. The dream of eternal youth turns into a nightmare when the original owners try to reclaim their lives permanently. In the end, you see that playing with life and death always has a price, leaving the couple in a tragic spot where they lose the very peace they paid for.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about futuristic tech and moral dilemmas.
